questions.prompt: Which of these is a power-block component?
options: A fuse and switch after the battery.
A TB6612FNG dual H-bridge motor driver.
An MPU-6050 inertial measurement sensor.
An ESP32 development board with Wi-Fi.
questions.explanation: A fuse and switch protect and control the energy source. The others are a driver, a sensor and a compute part.

questions.prompt: Which list names all six hardware blocks of a robot?
options: Compute, sensors, motors, battery, wires, software, firmware.
Sensors, memory, drivers, motors, a clock, cables, connectors.
Compute, sensors, drivers, actuators, power, communications.
Processor, camera, wheels, battery, charger, case, screws.
questions.explanation: The six blocks are compute, sensors, drivers, actuators, power and communications.

questions.prompt: Draw (describe) the block diagram of a 6-joint robot arm that uses smart serial-bus servos and a small PC. Name the six blocks, the interface on each link and one risk of the shared bus.
rubric: Places all six blocks: compute (PC and optional MCU or USB adapter), sensors and driver built into the servo, actuators, power (supply, fuse, regulator) and the bus.
Names the interface (half-duplex serial bus or USB-to-serial adapter) and the power path separate from the data path.
Names a shared-bus risk (message budget, one fault blocks all, termination, ID clashes) and checks it with a number.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: A wheel encoder reading ends up in a ROS 2 odometry message. Which order of stages is correct?
options: Encoder, ROS 2 node, MCU interrupt and counter, serial link.
Encoder, MCU interrupt and counter, serial link, ROS 2 node.
MCU interrupt and counter, encoder, ROS 2 node, serial link.
Encoder, serial link, MCU interrupt and counter, ROS 2 node.
questions.explanation: Pulses are counted by the MCU first; the counts are then packed and sent over the link; the ROS 2 node on the computer publishes the message.

questions.prompt: What kind of signal does a microcontroller typically send to a motor driver such as the TB6612FNG to set speed and direction?
options: Motor current at full battery voltage on the signal pin.
An analog voltage from a 12-bit ADC input pin.
I2C commands carried on the motor power wires.
PWM for speed plus logic pins for direction.
questions.explanation: The MCU only provides low-power logic. PWM sets the average motor voltage, and direction pins set the polarity; the driver switches the motor current.

questions.prompt: Why is it risky to run a 1 kHz motor current limit on a Linux single-board computer?
options: Linux cannot read digital input pins at any speed at all.
Scheduling can delay your code by random milliseconds.
Linux cannot send data over a USB port for robots.
Single-board computers cannot count up to 1000 per second.
questions.explanation: A general-purpose operating system is not hard real-time: other processes or interrupts can pause your task, so a time-critical safety loop belongs on the MCU.
questions.skillLabel: Choose MCU or SBC for a task

questions.prompt: Which task is the best fit for a Jetson Orin Nano class GPU module?
options: Generating a clean 20 kHz PWM waveform for a motor.
Counting quadrature pulses at 50 000 edges per second.
Cutting motor power within microseconds on a fault.
Neural-network object detection on camera frames.
questions.explanation: GPU modules are for heavy parallel compute such as vision networks. Pulse counting, PWM and instant fault reactions belong on MCU hardware.
questions.skillLabel: Choose MCU or SBC for a task

questions.prompt: A battery-powered sensor node samples one value per minute for a month. Which compute choice fits best?
options: A microcontroller that sleeps between samples.
A Raspberry Pi running Linux continuously all month.
A Jetson module with its GPU left mostly idle.
A laptop left running with the lid closed.
questions.explanation: A microcontroller can sleep at microamp-level currents (the ATmega328P datasheet lists tens of microamps in power-down); Linux boards draw far more.
questions.skillLabel: Choose MCU or SBC for a task

questions.prompt: An MPU-6050 belongs to which block, and why?
options: Driver, because it drives the I2C bus lines.
Actuator, because it contains moving parts.
Sensor, because it measures motion.
Compute, because it has a built-in processor.
questions.explanation: The MPU-6050 is an inertial measurement unit: it turns motion into digital readings sent over I2C.

questions.prompt: Which part is a communications block?
options: An RPLIDAR A1 laser scanner.
An MCP2515 CAN controller.
A 18650 lithium-ion cell.
A Pololu 37D gearmotor.
questions.explanation: The MCP2515 provides a CAN bus interface for an MCU. The RPLIDAR is a sensor, the 18650 a power part and the gearmotor an actuator.

questions.prompt: A 6-byte I2C burst read at 400 kHz (9 clocks per byte plus 3 address/register bytes). Time in microseconds.
questions.skillLabel: Bus time, latency and failure points

questions.prompt: An 8-byte message on a 57600 baud 8N1 UART. Time in milliseconds.
questions.skillLabel: Bus time, latency and failure points

questions.prompt: Latency stages: sample wait 4 ms, I2C 1.5 ms, processing 12 ms, serial 2 ms, controller 8 ms, driver and motor 15 ms. At 0.6 m/s, how many centimetres does the robot move during the total latency?
questions.skillLabel: Bus time, latency and failure points

questions.prompt: 8 joints on a 1 Mbit/s CAN bus, each cycle one command and one feedback frame per joint, 250 Hz, 111 microseconds per frame. Bus utilization as a fraction.
questions.skillLabel: Bus time, latency and failure points

questions.prompt: Which order lists the usual failure points of a new robot from most to least likely to check first?
options: Power, connectors and wires, ground, logic levels, timing.
Timing, logic levels, ground, connectors, power.
Software bugs, then compiler, then power.
Ground, timing, power, then logic levels, then connectors.
questions.explanation: Experienced builders check power and mechanical connections first because they are common and cheap to test, then ground, logic levels and timing.
questions.skillLabel: Bus time, latency and failure points

questions.prompt: A robot's Arduino resets whenever the motors start. Write a short, ordered debugging plan with the measurement you take at each step and how you decide which block is at fault.
rubric: Starts with power: measures the logic rail (multimeter or oscilloscope) while the motors start and checks the battery, fuse and wiring.
Isolates by bisection: runs the MCU alone, then adds the driver, then the motors, noting which step triggers the reset.
States a fix suited to the finding (separate regulator, bigger wire, capacitor) and a check that the reset no longer occurs.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
questions.skillLabel: Bus time, latency and failure points
